column8: Mon 16 Nov: store only; internal budget steps before late August that Laura cannot see; the late-May date is one year's description, not a statute.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a 2009 description of the old Council's March capital ceiling, current practice not re-checked.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e or Table 3 note: the statute behind the late-August first sight (Art. 46); used only with Q49-004's dates.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e or Table 3 note: the cabinet's draft each late August (13-26 Aug in seven years) is the one fixed first sight of Taiwan's public arts money; Table 3 has no room, so store unless a line is freed.
Mon 16 Nov: same late-August first sight as Q49-004; the Ministry's headline figure the same day adds only the 2026 number (2027 figures are Q10d-027).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; line items about two weeks after the draft, one year's posting date seen.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; UNVERIFIED (dates read from URL paths, NCAF's endowment share not read); verify before any use.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the Budget Center's November evaluations are a free source for Laura's watch, serving no report part.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e: the legal certain date (30 Nov, Art. 51); used only beside Q49-010, which shows it is not kept.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (3) and Table 3 row 7's note: public co-sponsor money is certain only at passage, which missed its legal date in 0 of 11 years (median about 20 Jan); widens Q10d's 351-day 2026 case into a record.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: adds the lapse risk (frozen items may never be spent) to Q10d-026's 351-day budget.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3e contrast in one clause: under Art. 54 new capital waits for the vote when Taiwan's budget is late, while Laura's owned Treasuries wait for no vote; a fact about co-sponsors' money, never Taiwan legal advice.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store beside Q10d-025: a voted grant can still sit frozen for months (building money frozen in FY2014).
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: cities and counties run the same calendar (to council by 30 Sep or 31 Oct, vote by 30 Nov); councils' on-time record not checked.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; one city's late-August letter of its central grants.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: site-specific public building money is often known only in late December and paid over two years; one office's book.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the 2026 shift to general grants, needed only to read Q49-019.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; named plan totals are budgets, not money paid.

Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 reading note: one bureau's 67% fall in 2026 was mostly a move into general grants, so the watch reads the general-grant line; 2026 was no recession (CANON B4); the line-by-line match was not traced.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d guard: the special forward-looking building budgets have expired, so never cite 2017-25 venue capital as money a residency could reach in 2031-33.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; Taipei's grant calendar.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; placemaking review months, result dates not found.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; local bureaus pay artists, not buildings; one county.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d contrast if room: public building money must be spent within its year or can be clawed back, while Laura's waits; store first.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and Table 3: public co-sponsors' 2033 money is first visible in late August 2032, about four months before Laura pays in December 2032, unlike private filings (Q30-031); passage usually comes after she pays; Keel arithmetic on verified dates.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 7 note line only if room is freed (Table 3 sits at one page with none): first seen late August, certain at passage, on time in 0 of 11 years.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3b: a private residency's public capital line is equipment-sized (at most NT$3m, about $91,550, shared with running costs), so Laura's capital is money public funders do not give a founder directly; fuller twin of Q9c-002.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d support for Q49-027: the equipment line is used (10 village grants, NT$12m, 2023).
Mon 16 Nov: same city-over-Ministry point as Q9c-019 (Treasure Hill, Ministry 5.8% of public money); adds only 2018's 15.5 times.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d support: Taipei's open grants pay no capital at all; one city.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: placemaking is the one public line where a private body asks for building money directly, at most NT$2m a year with public-use pledges; grant rules stay out of the report beyond one clause.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; private building money shrank within four years; Q10d-007's rule changes already carry the point.
Mon 16 Nov: context only: Taiwan has paid to reuse idle buildings for the arts since 1990; no part needs it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: a cabinet-approved building plan was cut and stretched as yearly budgets fell short in 2008-13; never told as a recession cut (CCA spending rose 29.1% in 2009, CANON B4); plan and outturn differ by source.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; phase 2 grants averaged about NT$1.6m with a local match; case counts conflict (1,452 against 1,473).
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 or 3d store: Taiwan's public building money could not pay staff (2009 rule, not re-read today), so owned running money does a job public capital cannot.
Mon 16 Nov: same Chishang hall case and source as Q51-036, which reads it rightly as a fit-out and repair gap; Fangliao F3 adds little.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: a city-run district's building money came as a decade of yearly grants, not one cheque.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; public capital at scale went to a city's flagship district, not a residency.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the one residency-space capital grant found, city applicant with a 30% match.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; residency-named public items are small and mostly running costs.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d support: every applicant on the forward-looking culture list is a city or county, so a founder reaches it only as a city's partner.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 or 3a store: a publicly built film centre sat idle over two years for want of an operator; reword the use, never the ten payments are the operations (H9-119: a base, not the whole budget).

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3e: Taiwan's named arts sponsorship set its record in the 2008-09 window (about NT$2.2bn, TAIEX -46%), so IPS l.9's cut is a risk for some co-sponsors, never all; fuller twin of Q4b-024; windows are Keel inference and part is Morakot giving.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: the 2008-09 peak has not been beaten (14th NT$2.04bn, 16th NT$1.87bn); fills Q12b-022's 15th; nominal figures.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 store: the only national sponsorship count dropped its money bands in 2025, so a 2031 check needs another source.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d scale: $115,000 = NT$3.77m (NUMBERS 8j) is a bronze-band sum; fix about 45-48 to 44-48 gold givers (15th and 16th editions); a two-year sum against a one-time contribution; never the largest share.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 support: NCAF's untied fundraising fell in 2008-09 and recovered in 2010, the channel where IPS l.9 holds; small sums.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3e store: NCAF's market income fell 37% short in 2008 and nearly doubled in 2009; never as Taiwan's government cutting arts money (its regular grants dipped about 6%, CCA spending rose 29.1% in 2009; CANON B4).
Mon 16 Nov: supporting data: TAIEX and GDP for 2008-09 read at source settle Q4b's UNVERIFIED figures; no part of its own.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3c evidence and a conceit turn for the judge: Taiwan's five-year arts pledge had 137 payers in year one, 46 in year five, none by year seven; use the counts, drop the 70% (unclear base, one 18-month period), and keep ink as owned in Treasuries, never paid money.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: in Taiwan's 2001 slowdown donors moved from a pooled fund to named projects; one institution's own account; the residency's fundraising design is cut from 3d.
Mon 16 Nov: same point as Q50-009 (named, matched projects raised money in the bad years); the NT$9m figure supports it.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: Taiwanese givers want results within the year, which frames the ten owned years as the long promise co-sponsors never make; recognition terms are cut from 3d.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3a parallel: the one multi-year gift NCAF could count on was paid on day one and booked a year at a time, as Laura's ten are owned before 2033; one anonymous gift.
Mon 16 Nov: NCAF's carry-forward entries are the accounting habit behind Q50-012; no separate use.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: Tung Ho Steel's three-year residency (2009-11), paid in kind, shows the multi-year form that survives a slump; one firm, not a facility gift; in-kind asks are not in the plan.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; award citations without amounts; long-term as renewal is read from citations only.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: firms renewed year by year; the 2009 step down may be project design, not the crash.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3e store: NCAF's flagship partners rotated in three- to four-year blocks, so expect one co-sponsor to change before 2033.
Mon 16 Nov: same NT$10bn fund promised in law and never reached as Q9-033, which is current to 2025 and says whose share was missing; adds only the 2010 figure.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 and CANON B4: a Taiwanese firm's arts budget follows this year's profit (p=0.007), not last year's, supporting IPS l.9's during that same period for corporate co-sponsors against Q4b's US lag; a 1999-2000 cross-section.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d support: Taiwanese firms said they cannot sponsor long-term, which fits the yearly programme ask from 2033 and the range never counting co-sponsors; survey before 2000.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d timing: meet co-sponsors before they set next year's budgets; the move before the meetings is unchanged; budget months not stated.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: foundations cap their total budget in a slump; abstract only.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: nine in ten Taiwanese foundations raise money to run programmes, so Q4b's US endowed-funder lag does not carry over; an old edition.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 store: most Taiwanese foundations publish little, so Laura can watch only what they disclose; press reports of the survey.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: in 2020 culture foundations' income held while spending fell 13.5%, a can't-spend shock, not a can't-pay one; different samples each year.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e support for CANON B4: Ministry subsidies to arts groups rose 79.6% in 2020 with relief and fell back in 2021, a boom year; 2021 is approved amounts, so never halved as like for like.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 store: listed firms' sustainability reports are a yearly source on corporate culture support before 2031.
Mon 16 Nov: out of scope beyond context: the culture-investment tax credit is a Taiwan tax matter (case p.4); store only.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e: Taiwan's arts' worst years (2020-21) were boom years for its shares, so co-sponsor risk follows the kind of shock; pairs with SKELETON 3e's 2009 supports it, 2020 does not; Laura's shares are VT, not the TAIEX.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: Taiwanese company giving (all causes) fell 3.3% in 2020 and rose 64.8% in 2021, following profit, not share prices; tax-adjusted figures.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; one industry drove 2021's jump; the label is Keel's alignment and the cause unread.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: Taiwan's private patrons are concentrated in the top fifth; the share-risk link is Keel inference.
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 or 3a store: households cut culture spending in the shutdown (9.53% to 6.34%), so a residency's earned income is the exposed line; the ten payments do not rest on it.
Mon 16 Nov: correction only: the Act is the 2021 rewrite, not a 2019 law; Taiwan legal and tax matters are out of scope, so cite it by its 2021 name if at all.
Mon 16 Nov: out of scope: Taiwan tax routing of gifts (case p.4); store only, never advice on how co-sponsors give.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; state firms appear among Wenxin winners, bands unchecked.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 store: the government's yearbook says 2008 hit Taiwan's creative industries hard; excerpt only.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e contrast: Korean and Australian firms cut sponsorship in 2008-09 while Taiwan's named totals rose; news reports of surveys.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3e store: campaigns that finish report about 108% of goal; self-selected respondents and a vendor, never a base rate.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: Kresge cancelled 0.2%-1.2% of a year's capital grants (2003-05), extending Q25-020; counts cancellations, not shortfall sizes.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: 9 of 119 small agencies missed a fixed-deadline match, a minority case for a co-sponsor falling short; endowment, not buildings.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e or 3d: in the 2008 crash about three-quarters of Kresge's capital grantees asked for more time; Laura's bottom, owned since January 2028 and stated in 2031, needs neither time nor money back.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3.0 store: in 2008 grantees most wanted bridge money between building and running; Laura's ten payments are a base bought in advance (H9-119); never suggest a bridge loan; adds to Q11b-022 and Q11b-023.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c or 3d store: at the AT&T Performing Arts Center the goal was raised and raised again, why Laura states one fixed top; a very large centre.
Mon 16 Nov: fix the use: non-local money in US arts buildings includes state and national grants, so it says nothing of a founder from abroad or who pays first; store only.
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 or 3a: NFF's 1994 base rate, close to a third of arts building projects left owners with serious long-term problems; the split between cushion and payments is Keel's mapping.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: 50-60% of projects borrowed; the plan borrows nothing; scanned text read as 50.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3b aha: the field's 1994 diagnosis is that arts managers lack early money and commit too soon; Laura's bottom is early money, owned from January 2028; pairs with aha 8 and never licenses a figure before it is owned.
Mon 16 Nov: same point as Q11b-023 (new buildings raise running costs that campaigns forget); 1994 wording only.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: funding was often set without cost estimates; supports stating dollars, never a facility estimate (out of scope).
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: surplus ratios fall after a facility project (matched sample); abstract only, read in full before use.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: 65% of $1-building groups saw budgets more than double; 17 hand-picked cases, and budget growth is not all facility cost.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: about half of small arts groups given cheap buildings ended financially weak; small sample, no comparison group.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: a practitioner's words, any cushion helps; one anonymous quote, and 3b's evidence line is already Klein 2001.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: most Philadelphia arts groups in expansion campaigns were thinly capitalised; one city, 2008.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b: US theatres locked their liquid capital into buildings (working capital negative for two-thirds); Laura's flexibility stays out of the building, in VT, promised to no one (IPS l.15); theatres, not residencies.
Mon 16 Nov: same point as Q9-010 (a cushion inside an operating budget gets spent); mixed results, no counts.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3d store: few nonprofits can raise facility reserves from funders, so a self-funded cushion is rare; all sectors, a mirror copy.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: US nonprofits running deficits rose from 13% to 37% (2021 to 2024); adds to H9-115; US, all sectors.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b illustration only (A31): owners paid about 12% of small Capital Works! projects; her flexibility is 25.9% times her unknown share s of the project, Keel arithmetic, never a plan figure.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b guard: Capital Works! gives both 78/57 and 57/78 for small and large projects, so store Q5d-016's 78% of small kept scope must be marked CONFLICTING; say a fifth to two-fifths cut scope.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: small projects took about 13 months; one collapsed scheme returned its grant; survey responses.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: liquidity improved for 45% of small owners against 90% of large; samples of 20 and 30, not attributable.
Mon 16 Nov: same rule as Q11c-019 (Arts Council England counts only 100% of other funding secured); a 2024 round repeats it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b and Table 3: without one public co-sponsor of about a fifth of cost, 48% of Canadian projects would not have happened, which sizes a co-sponsor falling short (IPS l.15); self-reported by grantees.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b: keep the fund's 10%-27% share of cost; drop only if she pays about 70% or more of the building, a figure solved for her unknown share s and not in NUMBERS (illustration only, A31).
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: the Cultural Spaces Fund approved 69% of applications (50% in 2022-23); a co-sponsor's own grant may not come.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: later phases are where projects break; fix paid in 2033 to the 2033 contribution paid in December 2032 (NUMBERS 4, 8j); never suggest paying in phases.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b: Washington's small projects still had a median 14% of goal to find after the state grant (a snapshot at award); drop her cushion is 13% if she pays half, a plan figure from the unknown s not in NUMBERS; state the yardstick with s named.
Mon 16 Nov: same Washington rules as Q11c-021 to Q11c-023 (over 50% raised, all other money bound, lapsing funds).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; small applicants returned for more, the reason unstated, so her own second round is Keel's reading.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: Massachusetts gives 24 months and may cancel; no cancellation counts; cash-in-hand rule already Q18-009.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 or 3a aha: of 399 subsidised Taiwan culture halls, 46 changed use or stopped by 2017, all 22 changes of use after subsidies ended; reword the use to ten years of her operating commitment, a base, not the whole budget (H9-119); public halls, not a private residency.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: Chishang's hall had money for the shell, none for fit-out or roof repair, and reverted; one case cited from a book; not Chishang's granary (Q11e-008).
Mon 16 Nov: 3b illustration only (A31): reopening idle Ministry buildings cost 5.8% of build cost; reopening is not finishing; 25.9% times s stays Keel arithmetic.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: lack of funds caused 13% of Taiwan's idle public facilities, so the plan secures money, not use; all public facilities.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store: a 14.5% late inflation top-up on a UK museum, 73% from the owner, as in Q5d-008; a large museum.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store: rising material costs brought a wave of grant-increase requests; no counts.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; UNVERIFIED (seen in a review's table); read Woronkowicz and Nicholson-Crotty in full before any use.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b illustration only (A31): keep her flexibility as 25.9% times her unknown share s, beside Q5d-030's overrun version; drop 13.0% at half and about the typical gap as plan figures not in NUMBERS; never to co-sponsors.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3e map: say what each part addresses (scope, debt, delay, trouble after opening) without claiming the plan answers each; flexibility a cushion, not a cure; the ten payments a base (H9-119); 22%-43% is a conflicting range.
